name: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: his birth name is given as Rūpa or Santoṣa in secondary sources; born c. 1489 (sources vary) in a Karnāṭa brāhmaṇa family settled in Bengal. Title at Husain Shah's court: Dabir Khās, chief secretary. Chief works: Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, Vidagdha-mādhava, Lalita-mādhava, Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi, Upadeśāmṛta. Traditionally left this world in 1564 at Sevā-kuñja, Vṛndāvana.

name: Śrī Śacī Devī
add: Nandgram Dham: her father Nīlāmbara Cakravartī was an astrologer and scholar of Navadvīpa; her husband Jagannātha Miśra came from Śrīhaṭṭa. Of her ten children two sons lived to adulthood, Viśvarūpa and Viśvambhara. Yaśodā (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 17.294); one of the four leading women Vaiṣṇavas of the Lord's own lifetime.

name: Sadāśiva Kavirāja
add: Nandgram Dham: the twenty-third of Nityānanda's listed devotees (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.38; Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 5.741); a vaidya, son of Kaṁsāri Sena, father of Puruṣottama dāsa Ṭhākura and grandfather of Kānu Ṭhākura. «Kavirāja» is a hereditary title of Vaidya families, shared with Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja and Govinda dāsa Kavirāja, who were of unrelated families. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Sadāśiva Paṇḍit
add: Nandgram Dham: the twelfth branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.34); his house in Navadvīpa was Nityānanda's first residence there. His birth and death are not recorded. Not Sadāśiva Kavirāja of Nityānanda's branch (Ādi 11.38).

name: Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: his birthplace is disputed between Naihāṭī, Bāklā-Candradvīpa / Fateyābād (Jessore) and Rāmakeli. His court post was Sākara Mallika under Husain Shah; his dīkṣā guru, Vidyāvācaspati, brother of Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. Chief works: Hari-bhakti-vilāsa, Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta, Bṛhad-vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī (Daśama-ṭippanī), Kṛṣṇa-līlā-stava. He left this world beside the Rādhā-Madana-mohana temple.

name: Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇa of Mathurā
add: Nandgram Dham: the Sanoḍiyā brāhmaṇas were priests of goldsmith and jeweller families. He met the Lord at the Ādi Keśava temple in Mathurā (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 17–18). His personal name is not recorded.

name: Santoṣa Datta
add: Nandgram Dham: some accounts call him Narottama's brother rather than his cousin. The Kheturī festival he paid for is traditionally dated 1574. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: chief royal paṇḍita of Vedānta at Pratāparudra's court; trained in Vedānta in Śaṅkarācārya's line. The Lord's seven days of Vedānta with him at Purī were early in 1510. Works: the Sārvabhauma-śataka (Caitanya-śataka) and the Advaitāṣṭaka. His disappearance is not recorded; he lived out his life in Purī.

name: Satyarāja Khān
add: Nandgram Dham: born Lakṣmīnātha Vasu; «Satyarāja Khān» is a court title. Father Guṇarāja Khān (Mālādhara Vasu), author of the Śrī Kṛṣṇa-vijaya; son Rāmānanda Vasu (not Rāmānanda Rāya). A kāyastha family that traced its coming to Bengal from Kānyakubja. The family supplied by inheritance the silk ropes for Jagannātha's Ratha-yātrā chariot.

name: Ser Khan
add: Nandgram Dham: also Sher Khān, Śera Khān; a Pathān official of the local Muslim administration in Orissa (deputy or ruler of the Ambua-Dhāreṇḍā pargana by one account); Dhāreṇḍā is on the Orissa–Bengal border, near Śyāmānanda's birthplace. Source: Prema-vilāsa 19 (Nityānanda dāsa); later 16th to early 17th century.

name: Śaṅkara Paṇḍit
add: Nandgram Dham: the eleventh branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.33), younger brother of Dāmodara Paṇḍita (the tenth). Called Prabhu-padopadhāna, «the Lord's foot-pillow»: his night service in Purī in the years of the Lord's most intense ecstasy. As Śrībhadrā, Kṛṣṇa slept on his chest in Vṛndāvana. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Viśvarūpa
add: Nandgram Dham: he left this world in 1431 or 1432 Śaka (1509 or 1510) at Paṇḍharpur, on the Bhīmā (Sholapur district); an incarnation of Baladeva, one with Saṅkarṣaṇa of the catur-vyūha (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 13.74).

name: Sāraṅga Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: also Sāraṅga Murāri, Śārṅga-pāṇi, Śārṅga-dhara. He worshipped Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Gopīnātha; Madana-Gopāla and Gaura-Gadādhara later joined the same altar.

name: Śikhi-Māhiti
add: Nandgram Dham: the eldest of the three; his post at the Jagannātha temple was Likhanādhikārī, «in charge of writing», keeper of the Mādalā Pāñji chronicle. Nandgram Dham counts him among the «three» of the three and a half, with Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāmānanda Rāya. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Śrī Śivānanda Sena
add: Nandgram Dham: the twenty-fourth branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.54); the people of Kulīna-grāma also joined his party to Purī. His wife is not named in the sources.

name: Śrīkānta Sen
add: Nandgram Dham: cousin of Śrīvallabha Sena; a kīrtana singer in Mukunda Datta's party at the Ratha-yātrā (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 10.63, Madhya 13.41, Antya 12.34–41). His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Śrīman Paṇḍit
add: Nandgram Dham: the fifteenth branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.37); the Lord's personal servant (nija-bhṛtya) and saṅkīrtana singer; also named in Madhya 10.83, 11.89 and Antya 10.9–11, 10.122. His birth and death are not recorded.
